article.title: Far-right student groups attack book exhibition with crude bomb
article.author: Abdul Rahman
article.content: A progressive book exhibition, organized by students of Calcutta University in India’s eastern state of West Bengal, faced a crude bomb attack by right-wing student organizations affiliated with the ruling ultra-right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), on Wednesday, November 18. The exhibition continued, even after the attack , which was allegedly carried out by the members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidhyarthi Parishad (ABVP), student wing of the Hindu supremacist organization Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh or National Volunteer Union (RSS), the parent organization of the BJP. A day earlier, security forces tried to stop the same exhibition and had attacked the book stalls set up by students and arrested several activists and leaders resisting their action. The attack by the security forces had prompted big protests by students, who accused the BJP-led state government of trying to censor books and crack down on the culture of dissent. Students have accused that Wednesday’s attacks were the result of the government shielding and promoting such violence against progressive books, cultural events, and university spaces. The protesting students have also demanded the release of activists arrested by the police on Tuesday. In a statement issued by the Student Federation of India (SFI), a left-wing student organization and the main organizer of the book exhibition, called the repeated attacks an assault on “democratic rights, freedom of expression, and the long-standing traditions of intellectual and political debate” in the state. The SFI and other left student groups organize book exhibitions in Kolkata’s College Street called “Literature of Struggle” every year to commemorate the 1917 October Revolution in Russia. The SFI claimed the attacks against them were part of the larger right wing turn West Bengal has taken, but reiterated its resolve to continue its resistance, despite the attacks. Rising intolerance towards freedom of expression The attacks on Tuesday and Wednesday were a continuation of similar attacks last month when the newly-formed BJP state government deployed bulldozers to demolish traditional progressive book stalls, organized every year during religious festivities. The BJP and ABVP activists have also been accused of attacking other book stalls and of launching a systemic attack on universities and cultural events in the state under police protection. The right-wing groups allege that progressive books, university spaces, and cultural events deliberately promote “anti-national” elements and ideas and must be stopped. The left organizations have called such reasoning a reflection of the BJP’s ideological intolerance of diversity and its fear of political dissent, with some even terming it “fascistic.” On October 31, thousands of people marched across the streets of Kolkata with books in hand to register their opposition to rising attacks on universities, freedom of expression, and cultural traditions in the state. The left student groups have also made a call for fresh mobilizations against such attacks on Friday, November 20.
